It resets the system, or a particular equipment, to factory configuration, stopping target traffic services and removing the respective files and user configurations, which may imply loss of connectivity; the clear is a secure wipe of system data. Target may be the entire system or a specific chassis or card AID; if no target is given the entire system is cleared. restart-behavior is either a standard restart (default) or shutdown, in which case the system does not restart afterwards, e.g. `clear system factory-reset shutdown`. Limits: factory-reset does not take effect on 1830 GX G30 Optical Carrier-Cards (OCC2T, OCC2E), it is supported on the G30 controller card (FRCU), and `clear system factory-reset` with the shutdown option is not supported on L0 cards. Other types are full-wipe and inactive; for a simple database wipe use `clear database`.

Run `time`. It is a bare command with no parameters and no flags that displays the system's time, available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Sample output: 2020-06-29T22:29:37+00:00. It reports the time based on the system configured timezone. For a fuller picture use `show clock`, which returns current-time, universal-time (UTC), timezone, uptime, uptime-seconds, time-source (ntp or manual), DST-active and last-time-jump, though note that if DNS is not properly configured `show clock` can take up to 2 minutes to return.

The `uptime` command displays system uptime and load average, for example: 21:24:09 up 41 days, 15:56, 1 user, load average: 0.10, 0.35, 0.39. The load average, also called average system load, indicates whether there are multiple tasks queued on the system (on the card). Whether it is high or low depends on the number of cores the system has, how many CPUs are integrated into the system/card, and the load average number itself. The rule stated is that a load average value is considered high when it is greater than the number of CPUs on the card. The command takes no parameters and runs in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. `show clock uptime` and `show clock uptime-seconds` give the uptime alone.

Yes. `manual-switchover [-f] [resource=]<value>` performs a manual switchover of the object identified by resource, given as an AID, and it prompts: 'Controller will switchover and connection to the management interface will be lost. Do you want to continue? [y/n]'. You confirm at that prompt to proceed, or use -f to force the command without confirmation. Examples per chassis: `manual-switchover card-1-3` on a 1830 GX G42, `manual-switchover card-1-5` on a G32, and `manual-switchover card-1-12` on a G34c. Access mode is Operational mode. For the full procedure, the guide points to the 1830 GX Software Management Procedures Guide.

`show protection`. It is a show-only command with no parameters that displays the protection setting, i.e. the node's protection container, and it runs in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. From there the individual objects are `show protection-group-<name>` for a protection group and `show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name>` for a member unit. The operating command for switching is `protection-switch`.

On protection-group, switching-mode takes unidirectional or bidirectional and defaults to unidirectional. The wait-to-restore timer is wtr-timer: trigger clearance soaking time before reverting to the working protection unit, measured and set in 1-second steps, range 60..720 seconds, default 300. It is only applicable in revertive mode, and reversion-mode itself takes revertive or non-revertive with a default of non-revertive, so you must set `set protection-group-<name> reversion-mode revertive` for wtr-timer to apply. remaining-wtr (show only, 0..720 seconds) reports the time left on the WTR timer. The separate hold-off-timer is the switching trigger soaking time before switching, measured and set in 1-millisecond steps, range 0..10000 ms, default 0.

Use the operating command `protection-switch [-f] [operation-type=]<value> [switch-target=]<value> [protection-group=]<value>`. operation-type takes force, lockout, manual or release; switch-target is the target of the switch and is not needed for the release and lockout operations; protection-group names the group. Example: `protection-switch protection-group-test operation-type=force switch-target=protection`. Use -f to force the command without confirmation. Access mode is Operational mode. The equivalent configured attribute is pg-request on the protection group, whose values are clear, manual-to-working, manual-to-protection, forced-to-working, forced-to-protection, protection-lockout and exercise (exercise applies only to bidirectional SNCP), with a default of clear.

Use `show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name>` and read the state attribute, whose values are active, standby, available and unknown; the unit reporting active is the one carrying traffic. The companion attribute role tells you whether that unit is the working or the protection member. The same show also returns AID, transport-entity (the transport entity instance identifier), alarm-report-control and label. At group level, `show protection-group-<name> pg-state` gives the switch state (no-request, wait-to-restore, forced-to-working, forced-to-protection, sf-on-working, and so on; default unavailable) and last-switch-trigger gives the reason for the last switchover. Only alarm-report-control (allowed, inhibited; default inhibited) and label are settable on a protection unit.

Most alarms have both an automatic raise and an automatic clear criteria, but a small subset have no clear criteria and require the user to acknowledge and clear them manually. Identify them with `show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true`, then clear with `clear [-f] alarm [alarm-type=]<value> [[resource=]<value>[,<value>]*]`, for example `clear alarm DBRESTOREFAIL`. Use -f to force the command without confirmation. This mechanism applies only to system alarms that are not associated with any particular resource but with the system itself, that is system-wide/global alarms. Access mode is Operational mode. To merely change operator state rather than clear, use `set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>...)` with state none, ack or close; the list takes 1 up to 10 alarm ids.

That is governed by the system-wide arc-behavior switch on alarm-control. `set alarm-control arc-behavior <value>` takes leave-alarms or clear-alarms, and the default is leave-alarms. With leave-alarms, when ARC is set to 'inhibit' the currently raised alarms are left in a raised mode; with clear-alarms, when ARC is set to 'inhibit' the current alarms are cleared. Check it with `show alarm-control`. The same command also carries alarm-soaking-behavior, values automatic (soaking time as defined in the FM profile) or no-soak (certain alarms specified in the FM profile have no soaking time), default automatic; note the OSC LOF alarm uses the per-facility user-configurable lof-soak-timer on the PBAx card. Access mode: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode. Per-object inhibiting is done with the alarm-report-control attribute (allowed, inhibited).

Use `show alarm-inventory-<alarm-type>`, e.g. `show alarm-inventory-TIM` or `show alarm-inventory-MSIM`. The alarm-inventory is the inventory of all possible alarm types for the system, holding static information per alarm type. The attributes are alarm-type-description (string 0..128), which explains what it means, and corrective-action (string 0..256), which is system provided information on how to correct the situation that triggered the alarm. It also gives resource-type, alarm-category (communication, facility, equipment, environmental, processing-error, software, quality-of-service, security), default-severity (critical, major, minor, warning, not-reported, event; the same alarm may have different default severities depending on the resource-type) and service-affecting (indeterminate, sa, nsa, sa-nsa). Access mode: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Yes, that is exactly what alarm-severity-entry is for: it configures the severity of one particular alarm. Use `set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <value>`, for example `set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor` or `set alarm-severity-entry-tom/EQPTCOMFAIL severity major`. resource-type is the resource being modified (CHM1R, FAN, 1830 GX G31, and so on), alarm-type is the abbreviated code (ADMIN-LOCK, BERSD, etc.), direction is na, ingress or egress, and location is na, near-end or far-end. severity takes critical, event, major, minor, not-reported or warning. Read it back with `show alarm-severity-entry-<...> [severity] [service-affecting]`, or `show alarm-severity-entry` for all entries; press '?' after the set command to list available entities. The object is system managed and cannot be manually deleted.

alarm-severity-profile assigns a severity to a whole profile rather than to a single resource-type/alarm-type/direction/location entry. Syntax: `set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <critical|event|major|minor|not-reported|warning>`, plus `show alarm-severity-profile`. profile-entry is the profile to be modified, and pressing '?' after `set alarm-severity-profile` lists the available profiles. Example: `set alarm-severity-profile alarm-severity-entry-trusted-certificate/CERTIFICATE-EXPIRED severity critical`. By contrast, alarm-severity-entry is keyed as <resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> and changes one particular alarm on one resource type, e.g. `set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor`. Both take the same severity value set, both run in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, and both objects are system managed and cannot be manually deleted.

Use `show current-alarms [number-of-alarms] [last-changed]`. number-of-alarms is the number of currently raised alarms, and last-changed is the timestamp of the last change in the current alarm list, covering either a raise or a clear event. Plain `show current-alarms` gives the list of currently raised alarms. Access mode: Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For a severity breakdown alongside other system information, the `status` (System dashboard) output carries an alarm summary, for example '13 current alarms (1 critical, 5 major, 2 not-reported, 5 minor)'. To inspect individual alarms use `show alarm-<alarm-id>` or `show alarms`.

Use the `get-conditions` command. A condition is an alarm that is not considered current, which happens when the alarm severity is configured as 'not-reported' or 'not-alarmed', when the alarm is suppressed due to alarm correlation, when it is suppressed due to ARC, or when it is suppressed due to AINS. Syntax: `get-conditions [[direction=]<value>] [[resource=]<value>] [[resource-type=]<value>] [[alarm-type=]<value>] [[location=]<value>] [[AID=]<value>]`. direction takes all, na, ingress or egress (default all) and location takes all, na, near-end or far-end (default all); resource, resource-type, alarm-type and AID are filters with no default. Access mode is Operational mode. Also check `show ne alarm-report-control` and the per-object alarm-report-control attribute, and `show alarm-severity-entry` for a severity set to not-reported.

Use set-alarm-state, which changes the operator state of an alarm and can also store user data in the alarm. Syntax: set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>[,<value>]*). state is mandatory and takes an operator-state of 'none', 'ack' or 'close'. Target either all currently raised alarms with all-alarms, or a list of alarm-ids with alarm-id-list, which accepts from 1 up to 10 alarm ids. acknowledge-text is optional and is a string of length 0..256 that is inserted as the acknowledge message. Setting a state that equals the current state is accepted, with only the text updated. Example: set-alarm-state ack all-alarms acknowledge-text=example. Access mode is Operational Mode.

Yes, use clear statistics: clear [-f] statistics [target=]<value>[,<value>]*. It clears the event counters (statistics) for the specified objects, where target is an instance-identifier and multiple targets can be listed. -f forces the command without confirmation, -h shows help. Scope is limited: the only currently supported object type is aaa-server, and AAA statistics are supported for TACACS+ servers but not for RADIUS servers. Clear everything for all AAA servers with 'clear statistics aaa-server', or a single server with 'clear statistics aaa-server-MyServer'. Access mode is Operational Mode.

Use show log with the -n and -t flags: show [-n=<number>] [-t] log [<logname> [exclude=<exclude-column> ...]]. -n=x limits output to the last x entries, and -t switches from the default CSV output (each column named in the header, matching the actual file content) to an aligned table display. So 'show -n=5 log security' gives the last 5 security entries, and adding -t aligns the columns. Table mode can become too wide, in which case drop columns with exclude=<column> after the logname (use <tab> auto-complete to list removable columns). Valid lognames include messages, linecard, shell-command, netconf-command, apps, cli-command, alarm, configuration, kernel, user, event, security and ztp. Output can be post-processed with piped commands, e.g. show log security | exclude john | include NETCONF. Note that due to system restrictions the security log may not be cleared.

Yes, that is expected: console logging is off by default. The log-console 'enabled' attribute switches console logging on and off, takes true or false, and defaults to false. Turn it on with 'set log-console enabled true' and check with 'show log-console'. The other log-console attribute is source-facilities, the list of syslog facilities used in this configuration, chosen from all, authentication, clock-daemon-15, clock-daemon-9, ftp-daemon, kernel, line-printer, local1 through local7, log-alert, log-audit, mail-system, network-news, ntp, security, syslog-internal, system-daemons, user-level and uucp. Access mode is Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode.

Add a log-console-facility-filter, a selector that filters console messages on source facility and severity: add log-console-facility-filter-<name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. The <name> identifies a single syslog facility, or all of them if the value is 'all' (kernel, user-level, authentication, security, local1..local7, ntp, etc). severity takes emergency (level 0), alert (1), critical (2), error (3), warning (4), notice (5), informational (6) or debug (7), and defaults to informational. compare-op controls how the comparison is made: equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals, defaulting to equals-or-higher. To show only serious messages: add log-console-facility-filter-all severity 'critical'. Use set to change it, show to view, delete to remove it.

Local retention is governed by two log-file attributes. max-file-size is the maximum file size before rotation, a uint8 in the range 1..30 megabytes, defaulting to 30. number-of-files is the maximum number of log files retained, a uint8 in the range 1..20, defaulting to 10; when rotating files because max-file-size was reached, the oldest files are discarded once the total number exceeds number-of-files. So by default the node keeps up to 10 files of up to 30 MB each. Set them with add/set log-file-<name> [number-of-files <value>] [max-file-size <value>]. The name is the file name without the .log extension, string length 0...128. Locally saved log files can be emptied with clear or removed with delete, but the default system log file cannot be edited or deleted.

Yes. Restrict the file to the authentication facility with the log-file source-facilities attribute, which is the list of syslog facilities used in that configuration and defaults to all: add log-file-authlog source-facilities authentication. Facility 4 is named 'authentication' in the CLI and carries authentication/authorization attempt messages (facility 10, 'security', carries security related events and error messages). You can then narrow by severity per facility with add log-file-facility-filter-<log-file-name>/<log-file-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>], where severity is one of emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, informational, debug (default informational) and compare-op is equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals (default equals-or-higher). By default severity is set to informational and above.

Configure the collector with add log-server-<name> address <IP address> ... port <value> transport <udp|tls|tcp>. Unless you say otherwise, port defaults to 514 (range 1..65535) and message-format defaults to rfc5424 (the alternative is rfc3164). transport defaults to udp, so for TLS you must set transport tls explicitly. Other defaults: enabled true, message-coalescence true, origin manual, source-facilities all, destination-facility-override disabled (otherwise a facility number in range 0..11 or 16..23), sensitive-data none (none, only, both), alarm-report-control allowed. name is a string of length 0...64, address may be IPv4, IPv6 or a DNS domain name, and pattern-match is a regular expression string of length 0..255.

Yes, use log-server-facility-filter: add log-server-facility-filter-<log-server-name>/<log-server-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. It filters log messages based on their source facilities and severities for that one server. It cannot widen what is sent: the filter is based on the source-facilities leaf-list and can only add a filter to the already configured source facilities. The filter name identifies a single syslog facility, or all of them if the value is 'all' (kernel, user-level, mail-system, system-daemons, authentication, syslog-internal, line-printer, network-news, uucp, clock-daemon-9, security, ftp-daemon, ntp, log-audit, log-alert, clock-daemon-15, local0..local7). severity takes emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, informational or debug, default informational; compare-op takes equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals, default equals-or-higher. Example: add log-server-facility-filter-server184/local2 severity debug.

Use the global syslog switch: set syslog remote-logging-switch false. That flag, when false, disables all remote logging destinations, and it defaults to true; the configured log-server entries stay in place. Verify with 'show syslog remote-logging-switch'. Related syslog attributes are source-address (address or hostname inserted in the HOST field, default localhost), log-file-message-coalescence (default true), log-relay (enables remote logging from a shelf controller to a node controller, default false), assignment-method (both, manual or dhcp, default both), niap-compliant-logging (default false), privacy-mode (GDPR filter, default false), alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default allowed) and label (string 0..256). Access mode is Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode.

The shared-secret of an aaa-server has a maximum length of 64 characters; any value longer than 64 characters is denied with an error message (the parameter table lists the type as String, length 0...128). Its default value is 'sharedkey' and it is always displayed as *. Set it with add/set aaa-server-<server-name> ... [shared-secret <value>]. Related aaa-server values: server-name is a string of length 1...64, protocol-supported is RADIUS or TACACSPLUS (default RADIUS), server-port defaults to 49, server-port-authentication 1812, server-port-accounting 1813, timeout is 1..90 seconds (default 5), and retry is 0..5, with total wait time timeout x (retry + 1) required to be less than 5 minutes.

That is expected behaviour, not a bug. In show aaa-statistics-<server-name>, the authentication-requests counter displays the number of authentication requests, and for TACACS+ the default authentication protocol includes both PAP and CHAP. The counter tracks each retry and each authentication protocol attempted independently, so authentication requests may increase by 2 for each retry. The command is only for AAA servers that use the TACACS+ protocol, and also exposes connection-failures (failures due to unavailable servers and timeouts), authentication-rejects, authorization-requests, authorization-rejects and accounting-requests, all integers. Reset them with 'clear statistics aaa-server-<name>'.

If you omit action on an ace, the default action taken by the filter is drop (the other values are accept and reject). An ACL must already exist before an ACE can be added, and at least one of source IP, destination IP, L4 ports, TTL or protocol must be provided. Limits: sequence-id, which sets the relative order of the ACE within the ACL, has range 1-100 for AUX and DCN-B interfaces and 1-256 for the DCN-A interface, and it is recommended to use multiples of 5 so rules can be inserted later. A maximum of 16 ACEs can be created on an ACL if both upper-port and lower-port values are specified; adding a 17th such ACE returns an error message. Other defaults: direction input, logging-action false, protocol any, ttl 255 (range 1...255), source/destination lower and upper port 0. Example: add ace-TrafficV6/100 action drop source-ip-address 2420::5.

Create the filter with add acl-<name> type <value> interface <value> [admin-state <value>]. The interface is the interface the filter is applied to, and the available values are 1-AUX-1, 1-AUX-2, DCN, DCN-B, DCN-2 and DCN-2-B (use 'add acl-name interface ?' to list them). An ACL can be added on the DCN-B interface when the DCN is operating in active-active configuration. Yes, IPv6 is handled: the mandatory type attribute indicates the top-level type of ACL, i.e. which fields of the associated IPv4 or IPv6 header the ACL matches on, and takes IPv4 or IPv6. name is a string of length 0...30 and admin-state takes lock, maintenance or unlock, defaulting to unlock. An ACL can have one or more ACEs. Example: add acl-AuxV4traffic interface 1-AUX-2 type ipv4.

Yes: show access-control-list. It is a show-only command used to display the access control list, and it takes no parameters. Access mode is Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode. For the per-list detail use 'show acl-<name> [admin-state] [oper-state] [avail-state] [type] [interface]' and for the individual entries 'show ace-<name>/<sequence-id>'.

Add an access-rule with action deny inside an access-rule-list: add access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name> action <value> [sequence-id <value>] [module-name <value>] [path <value>] [attribute <value>] [attribute-value <value>] [operation <value>] [description <value>]. action is mandatory whenever a rule is created and takes permit or deny. path is the target object, an XPath of a YANG data node, notification, RPC or descendant, or an external command, max length 255, default '*'. operation is a bits value from create, read, update, delete, execute, default '*'; write access covers create/update/delete. Example denying creation of a card: add access-rule-1/rule path /ne/equipment/card operation create action deny. The rule list is scoped to user-groups via access-rule-list. module-name defaults to '*', attribute and attribute-value are leaf-lists of up to 10 strings of max 64 characters. The system supports a maximum of 500 access-rules across all access-rule-lists.

Order is by sequence-id: the access-rule-list is processed in order as given by sequence-id, and lower number ids are processed first. If sequence-id is not provided it is set to the currently used latest id plus 1, so the entry goes to the end of the list; the id is a uint16 and can be changed over the lifetime of the list to re-sort entries. Scope the list to groups with the user-group attribute on add/set access-rule-list-<name>: it is a leaf-list of user-group names, the default value '*' matches all existing user-groups, and a maximum of 20 user-groups can be referenced. description is a string of length 0..256. Example: add access-rule-list-A user-group XY.

Despite the name it is OSPF-specific: auth-key adds, edits or shows an authorization key whose 'key' attribute is the pre-shared key for OSPFv3 IPsec integrity protection. The AID is fully OSPF-scoped: add auth-key-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<spi> key <value> [type <value>], where instance-id is the OSPF instance ID (range 0..255), ospf-area-id is the OSPF Router Area ID, ospf-if-name references the interface in the OSPF area, and spi is a unique security parameter index for the SA in range 256..4294967295. key is a string of length 8..128 and type indicates whether the integrity key is ASCII or hexadecimal encoded (ascii, hex). Example: add auth-key-1/0.0.0.0/DCN/256 key abcdefgh12345678.

Set the global authorization mode to rules-only: set authorization mode rules-only. mode selects which kind of authorization rules are used: static-only (only system defined static rules), static+rules (both user and system defined access-rules, with a user configured access-rule tried first and system rules as fallback) and rules-only (only user defined access-rules, falling back to the global defaults if no rule matches). The default mode is static+rules. In rules-only mode the fallbacks read-default, write-default and exec-default become configurable, each permit or deny; read-default defaults to permit (get/show and receiving notifications), write-default defaults to deny (create/update/delete) and exec-default defaults to permit (RPC and command invocation). To deny anything not covered, set them to deny, e.g. set authorization write-default deny. show authorization also reports denied-operations, denied-data-writes and denied-notifications.

A user changes their own password with the password command: password [old-password=<old-password>] [new-password=<new-password>]. Both the current/old and the new password must be provided, and this is supported only for local users. Run it with no arguments for interactive input, where the passwords are prompted, not echoed, and the new one must be typed twice to confirm (Ctrl+C cancels); or provide them inline for scripts and automation, e.g. password old-password=Infinera4u! new-password=Infinera4us!. Inline, the special characters \" and ' must be escaped with \ and #?|; must be enclosed in single or double quotes. A password may contain up to 200 characters. To reset another user's password, an admin uses 'set user-<username> force-password-change true', which forces that user to change their password at next login. Access mode is Operational mode.

Use 'show security'. It is the show-only command for the top level security container and takes no parameters; access mode is Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode. Below it, 'show security-policies' displays the individual policy flags (secure-mode, strict-password-check, minimum-password-length, ssh and TLS algorithm lists, and so on).

minimum-password-length is the configurable minimum length for user passwords, a number in range 1..200 with a default of 8; the length is verified against this policy whenever a password is changed. Password history is controlled by enforce-password-history-check (true or false, default true), which ensures a new password cannot match any of the previous 5 passwords for that user, and by password-history-size, the number of passwords stored for reuse checking, a number in range 1..200 with a default of 5. strict-password-check defaults to true and enforces minimum length 8, at least one lower case letter, one upper case letter, one number and one symbol, and forbids the user name being part of the password; if disabled only a minimum length of 1 character applies. Both these policies only affect newly defined passwords once enabled. Set them via set security-policies.

Per user, max-invalid-login is the maximum number of consecutive invalid login attempts before an account is suspended (locked out); it is a number in range 0-255 and defaults to 5. suspension-time is the duration of UID suspension following those consecutive invalid login attempts, in minutes, range 0 - 1440, defaulting to 5 minutes. Set them with add/set user-<user-name> [max-invalid-login <value>] [suspension-time <value>]. 'show user-<name>' reports user-status, where 'lockout' means the account is locked out due to unsuccessful login attempts, and failed-logins, the number of previous failed logins, which resets to zero upon a successful login. Lockout can be turned off globally through the security-policies disable-user-lockout attribute.

user-data is a show-only command: 'show user-data'. It takes no parameters and displays the user-data. Access mode is Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. For per-user attributes use 'show user-<user-name>' instead, which exposes user-group, display-name, max-invalid-login, suspension-time, timeout, password-aging-interval, password-expiration-date, enabled, user-status, force-password-change, max-sessions, last-login-date, failed-logins, user-aaa-type, alarm-report-control and label.

Use add user-group-<name> [description <value>]. The group name is a String of 1...64 characters and the description, a long description of the user group, is a String of 1...128 characters. Each user is associated with a list of groups and derives its permissions from them, so a group is what you hang access-rule-lists and permissions off. Manage it with set user-group-<name> [description <value>], show user-group-<name> [description] and delete user-group-<name>. Example: add user-group-XY. The system already provides EA (Encryption Administrator), MA (Monitoring Access), NA (Network Administrator), NE (Network Engineer), PR (Provisioning), SA (Security Administrator) and TT (Turn-up and Test); 'show user-group' lists them with their descriptions. Access mode is Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode.

Add/Drop Groups are addressed as adg-<adg-number>, where adg-number is an integer in the range [1..110], so a node can have up to 110 ADGs (this matches oadm-capabilities max-adgs = 110). Use 'add adg-1', 'set adg-<n> label <value>', 'delete adg-<n>'. Wavelength duplication is reported by the read-only attribute wavelength-duplication, shown with 'show adg-<n> wavelength-duplication'. Its values are one-per-adg (default: no duplication of frequencies in the ADG) and one-per-degree (CDC: duplication of frequencies allowed in the ADG, but only one at the Degree). Only CDCs allow more than one instance of the same wavelength on the ADG. Other show-only attributes are max-add-drop-ports and bands-supported (default standardC-band). Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Gain is requested with 'set amplifier-<name> gain-target <value>', range 0..40 dB, default 0.0, applicable for manual control mode (control-mode = manual; the default is auto-max-pw, the auto mode targeting maximum output power). In auto mode you instead use gain-adjustment, range [-20.00..20.00], default 0, supported only on amplifiers whose function is 'pa' or 'inline'. gain-operating reads back the actual gain (0..40 dB). Tilt is controlled by tilt-control-mode: auto (default, system controls tilt per configured fiber parameters), auto-planned (per planning tool parameters), or manual. So the system controls tilt by itself unless you select manual; when amplifier function is 'add' or 'drop' the only option is manual. tilt-target ([-5..5] dB, default 0 dB) applies in manual mode and warns that the attribute may be traffic affecting; tilt-adjustment ([-5..5] dB, default 0 dB) offsets the target in auto/auto-planned.

Use 'set amplifier-raman-<name> target-raman-gain <value>'. The permitted range is [0, 5..30 dB] with default 0 dB, that is 0 or a value from 5 to 30 dB. It is configurable only when control-mode is different from auto; if control-mode is auto the parameter is ignored (control-mode values: auto (default), auto-planned, manual; in auto you configure only the span attributes, in auto-planned you configure the target Raman gain plus span attributes, in manual even the target pump powers must be configured). Pump count is read with 'show amplifier-raman-<name> number-of-pumps'; its values are 4 or 2 for the required-equipped card, and that value dictates the number of pump-power objects exposed by the system. Related read-backs: total-pump-power ([-99..99] dBm, -99 means no power), actual-raman-signal-gain and actual-raman-osc-gain (0 when the amplifier is disabled).

Switch it on with 'set ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-enable enabled' (for example 'set ase-idler-service-1-8 ase-idler-enable enabled'); the attribute can also be given on 'add ase-idler-service-<name>'. Values are enabled and disabled, default disabled: enabled turns on ASE idler signal filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum. To see whether it actually came up, read the show-only attribute ase-idler-state: ase-enabled (ASE idler signal filling is complete on the band spectrum), ase-partially-enabled (filling incomplete), ase-faulted (ASE idler signal is faulted) and ase-disabled (default, signal completely removed from the band spectrum). 'show ase-idler-service-<name>' also gives oper-state (default disabled), avail-state, function (idler) and alarm-report-control.

'set ase-idler-source-<name> target-output-power <value>' takes a value in the range (-3.00..20.50) dBm, default 13; it is the ASE pump output power required when manually configured. The pump is not on by default: pump-enable has values enabled and disabled with default disabled, so you must set it explicitly. Example from the guide: 'set ase-idler-source-1-3.1-ase pump-enable 'enabled' target-output-power '15.00''. The actual pump status is read back through the show-only pump-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled). Other settable attributes are admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), label (0..256 characters) and alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed). function is fixed at ase-idler-source. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the calibrate command, available in Operational Mode only. Syntax: calibrate [type=]<value> [trigger=]<value> [entity=]<value>. type has a single value, raman, which triggers calibration on raman cards. trigger is start (starts the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span) or stop (stops it). entity is an instance-identifier selecting the entity to be calibrated; for raman calibration the entity may be an OTS-R entity. To start: 'calibrate raman start ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line'. To stop: 'calibrate raman stop ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line'. None of the three parameters has a default, so all must be supplied.

A degree is addressed as degree-<degree-number> with degree-number an integer in the range [1..20]; it must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees, and oadm-capabilities reports max-degrees = 20. Create with 'add degree-1', remove with 'delete degree-<n>', label with 'set degree-<n> label <value>'. The spectral grid is reported by show-only attributes: slot-width-granularity, the width of a slot, default 6250 MHz; center-freq-granularity, the granularity of allowed center frequencies, default 3125 MHz, with base frequency 193.1 THz per G.694.1; min-slots, the minimum number of slots that may be joined to form a media channel, default 8; and max-slots, the maximum, default 32 (min-slots must be less than or equal to max-slots). bands-supported defaults to standardC-band. Also shown: is-foadm (default false) and wss-less (default true).

On a multi-rail ILA node the system pairs indices with the two line ports of each ILA card. Direction n and direction n+1 are automatically assigned by the system to the DWDM Line1 and DWDM Line2 ports of the #n C2ILASGH/D2ILASGM card created, where index n is an odd integer with a value between 1 and 15. DWDM Line1 is always assigned an odd index value and DWDM Line2 always an even index value, which is why directions come in odd/even pairs. The index range is [1..16] (1 and 2 are used when migrating from R6.x). The system sets direction-number to 1 when direction-port is dwdm-line1 and 2 when it is dwdm-line2, and fills direction-card as card-<chassis>-<slot>. The same dwdm-line* port instance of an ILAx can only be selected once per NE. Use 'add direction-<index> direction-port port-<shelf>-<slot>-dwdm-line1' and 'delete [-f] direction-<index>', where -f forces without confirmation.

On a dsc facility you can configure only three attributes, on both 'add dsc-<name>' and 'set dsc-<name>': label (string 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default allowed). The name is a string of length 0..128. Everything else is show-only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by. managed-by describes whether this facility was system created or not, with values system (the default) and user; the stated consequence is that only user-created facilities can be user deleted, so a dsc reported as managed-by system cannot be removed with 'delete dsc-<name>'. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

On dsc-group (both add and set) the pre-FEC threshold is pre-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold, the threshold on which the PRE-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE alarm is raised: decimal64 with 3 fraction digits, range 0 or 5.600..9.600 dB, where 0 disables threshold crossing alarming and the specific sub-range is per carrier use-case. Its hysteresis, pre-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis, is 0.1..1.0 dB with default 0.5. The post-FEC threshold is post-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold for the POST-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE alarm: decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range 12.5..18.0 dB, default 18. Its hysteresis, post-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis, is 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. Related on the same object is dgd-high-threshold for the DGD-OORH alarm, uint16 range 25..400 ps, default 100. Example: 'add dsc-group-1-3-1-1 rate 100 carriers 1-3-1 group-id 1 instance-id 1'.

Use the gadt command, which retrieves golden carrier application information from the Golden Application Descriptions Table. Syntax: show gadt [<application-description-H|application-description-P|application-description-S|application-description-U>]. Each of the four attributes is a string giving the detailed description of that application ID, and none has a default. Example: 'show gadt application-description-H' returns application-description 'Subsea modes using Uniform and Hybrid modulation'. Running 'show gadt' with no attribute lists them all. Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. The application ID letters H, P, S and U are the same ones that appear as the application field of a golden carrier mode such as 800M.95P.

gapt lists the golden advanced parameters from the Golden Advanced Parameters Table (GAPT). It is scoped per card type: the syntax is 'show gapt-<card-type> [version] [applicable-resource-type]', where card-type is a string naming the card. 'show gapt' with no instance lists the tables that exist, for example gapt-CHM6 with version 1.8, gapt-CHM7 with version 3.0 and gapt-CHM7T. 'show gapt-chm7' lists that card type's individual parameters as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/<name> entries (BOASetting, CRAvgNCtrl, ClockPreEmphasis, EEPNNLMitigation, NLC, PDLMitigation, RxCDMode, RxRollOff, TxHighFreqGain and others) plus version and applicable-resource-type. version is a string of length 0..5 giving the table version; applicable-resource-type names the managed resource type(s) applicable for that advanced parameter. Show only, in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the gcmt command, which retrieves information about the golden carrier mode. Syntax: show gcmt [<card-type>] [version]. To look up a specific mode, name the golden carrier mode object: 'show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P'. The output row is keyed by the card-qualified instance, for example golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P, and gives capacity (Gbps) 800, client-mode ethernet-otn, baud-rate (GBaud) 95.2965203, application P, compatibility-id 6 and status supported. version returns the table version. For the full per-attribute detail of one mode, use the related command 'show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode>', which exposes actual-carrier-mode, capacity, client-mode, baud-rate, application, compatibility-id, status, sop-tracking-mode, supported-subtypes and candidate-subtypes. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read the status attribute, which describes the carrier mode release status. Use 'show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> status', where carrier-mode is a string of 1..15 characters in the format <Capacity><ClientMode>.<Baud Rate><Application ID>, for example 600E.84P, 100X.73U or 325M.66P. The permitted status values are supported, candidate, experimental, deprecated and diagnostic, so a mode is fully supported only when status is supported, and experimental marks the trial ones. Two related attributes qualify this per subtype: supported-subtypes lists the subtypes each carrier mode supports (strings of length 0..32, maximum 20 elements) and candidate-subtypes lists the subtypes for which this carrier mode has candidate status (strings of length 0..16, maximum 10 elements). The status column is also shown in the summary output of 'show gcmt'.

The command is l0-capabilities, which shows the capabilities details related with the node's Layer 0 functions. Syntax is simply 'show l0-capabilities'; the command takes no parameters. It is available in both Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For the photonic node dimensioning limits specifically, the companion command is 'show oadm-capabilities', which reports max-degrees (20) and max-adgs (110).

Creating a Media Channel requires three mandatory arguments: 'add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value>', with optional label, admin-state, alarm-report-control and auto-delete. lower-frequency and upper-frequency are values in MHz. parent-oms is an instance-identifier and is only set upon MC creation; the referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree and cannot be in an ADG. The system derives center-frequency (MHz) and slot-width, calculated as upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. auto-delete has values disabled (default) and enabled; when enabled the system automatically deletes the MC once the NMC associated with it is deleted, and it may only be enabled on RD66TM sleds (l0-mode-op=hsc-ols). Example: 'add mc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 parent-oms '1-3.1-dwdm-line' lower-frequency '192225000' upper-frequency '192300000''.

The Media Channel Filler is read only. The mc-f command supports only show: 'show mc-f-<name> [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [AID] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [slot-width]'. There is no add, set or delete form, and every parameter in the table is marked as used in show only. name is a string of length 0..64; lower-frequency and upper-frequency are the lower and upper frequencies of the MC Filler in MHz units; slot-width is calculated by the system from upper-frequency minus lower-frequency, also in MHz. supporting-card and supporting-port are leafrefs to the card and port holding the facility, and AID is the Resource Access Identifier (string 1..64). Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. The related Network Media Channel Filler, nmc-f, does allow a limited set of admin-state and alarm-report-control.

Up to four cards per ADG: 'add modules-adg-<adg-number>/<index> supported-card <value> [ocm-monitoring <value>]', where adg-number is in the range [1..110] and index is a number in the range [1..4]. The card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is an instance identifier for the card assigned to the ADG. Channel monitoring is on by default: ocm-monitoring has values true and false with default true. It is set upon creation and cannot be changed after supported-card has been assigned, and it can optionally be configured to false for OMD cards directly connected to PAx/BAX or C2ILASGH degrees, for example FOADM nodes. Example: 'add modules-adg-1/1 supported-card card-1-6'. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode; user access privilege Network Administrator or Network Engineer.

Use the modules-degree command: 'add modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>', for example 'add modules-degree-1/1 supported-card card-1-1'. degree-number is a number in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. index has the single permitted value 1, and the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is an instance identifier for the card or subcard that belongs to the degree; in R6.0 the card must be RD09SM or RD20TM. You can afterwards use 'set modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> [supported-card <value>]', 'show modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> [supported-card]' and 'delete modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index>'. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode; user access privilege Network Administrator or Network Engineer.

Use 'show monitored-channel-<name>/<frequency> monitored-optical-power', for example 'show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 monitored-optical-power'. The name corresponds to the (WS04S) card name with the suffix -1 or -2, for ocm1-in or ocm2-in respectively, and frequency is the nominal center frequency of the carrier (channel) in MHz as a uint32. monitored-optical-power is the measured power for the corresponding carrier in dBm, decimal64 in the range (-99.00..99.00), default -99, where -99.00 means no power. The other attribute available is monitored-width, a uint32 default 0, which is the carrier (channel) width configured at the NMC within the oxcon source or destination, in MHz. Omitting the attribute name, as in 'show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500', displays both. The command is show only, in Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On 'add nmc-<name>' the nominal center-frequency is mandatory and takes values in the range [190650000..196700000] MHz. width is the Network Media Channel frequency width in MHz, with values in the range [15000..200000] MHz and default 35000. The user must configure the 3 dB signal bandwidth, and the value in GHz must be equivalent to the baud rate in GBd configured on the connected transponder line interface line port. Both center-frequency and width are set at add time and are show-only afterwards. The other mandatory add argument is parent-facility, which can be either a Media Channel or an OMS, is only set upon creation, and whose referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree and cannot be in an ADG. Example: 'add nmc-cdc-1-4_192800000-34000 center-frequency 192800000 width 34000 parent-facility oms-1-4-ad1'.

The Network Media Channel Filler occupies 75000 MHz by default: alloc-bandwidth, the allocated bandwidth of the NMC Filler, is a value in MHz units with default 75000, bounded by alloc-lower-frequency and alloc-upper-frequency. The actual occupancy is reported separately by actual-bandwidth (MHz, default 0) with actual-lower-frequency and actual-upper-frequency. It is monitored: monitoring-state indicates whether the NMC is intended to be in use, has values enabled and disabled, and because it is a system created attribute it is enabled by default. Power read-backs are power-actual-tx and power-actual-rx, both [-99.00..99.00] dBm with default -99. Only admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed) are settable via 'set nmc-f-<name>'. Example: 'show nmc-f-1-3-dwdm-line-58'.

Run 'show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs]'. max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees, reported as 20 (uint8), and is 0 if not supported; degrees are only supported in OADM node types, and the maximum degrees for ILA node-type is 0 by convention since an ILA has only 2 directions, fixedly, which is not shown in supported capabilities. Note that the maximum number of Degrees is not necessarily the deployment supported configuration, but the maximum number of a working degree-number. max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups, reported as 110 (uint8), and is 0 if not supported; ADGs are also only supported in OADM node types. Sample output: max-degrees 20, max-adgs 110. Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. These bounds match the degree-number range [1..20] and adg-number range [1..110].

On 'set oc-<name>' the loopback attribute takes facility, terminal or none, with default none, and is described as useful to debug on the fiber connection. A companion attribute loopback-mode indicates the loopback action for facility or terminal, with values facility and terminal and no default. For test patterns, test-signal-type is the type of test pattern that is injected, with values none, enumeration, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9 and PRBS31, default none. test-signal-direction has the single value ingress, which is also the default. test-signal-monitoring, true or false with default false, monitors the incoming test signals for diagnostics. Example: 'set oc-1-5-T9.1 test-signal-monitoring false'. Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

In ILA nodes the OCHm represents the signaled optical channel from OSC, detected at the ILA OMS by using the OSC information. Consequently, when either the OMS monitoring-mode is not-monitored (as configured by the user), or there is no OSC messaging information, the list of OCHm facilities in the NE will be empty. Read it with 'show ochm' or 'show ochm-<name>', for example 'show ochm-1-7-dwdm-line2-191968750-egress avail-state'. direction is show-only, values ingress and egress, default egress, and only Egress is currently supported. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, default -99, where -99 dBm means the power is not yet measured (measurement is performed by the OCM at DGE2 card) or no power is detected; for egress it is calibrated at the DWDM Line port output. target-actual-power and attenuation-actual apply to HSC OLS nodes. Only label, admin-state and alarm-report-control are settable.

Use the ocm-channel command. It lists the detected carriers within the configured OXcon(s) and is show-only: show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency> [opm-pwr] [connected]. The key is the entity name (String, length 0..64) plus lower-frequency and upper-frequency, both uint32, which are the lower and upper frequency of the corresponding spectrum power (OPM-pwr point). opm-pwr reports the Optical Parameter Monitor power in dBm, decimal64 in range -99.00..99.00 with default -99. connected yields 'true' if the channel is configured, that is, involved in an oxcon; values true/false, default false. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Yes. On the ocm-mp facility the attribute ocm-enable, which enables regular power monitoring, takes values disabled or enabled with default enabled. Turn it off or on with set ocm-mp-<name> ocm-enable <disabled|enabled>. The only other settable attributes are label (String 0..256) and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). Read-only companions include monitoring-state, which the system reports as enabled when an OMS reference exists (values enabled/disabled, default enabled); monitored-port, the port actually being monitored, which can differ from supporting-port for a non-integrated OCM (default not-applicable); and ad-direction, which for ocm-mp is only ingress. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

The ocm-ptp facility is available for WS04S cards within a CD-AD ADG and provides dedicated OCM monitoring. It is not enabled out of the box: ocm-enable (enabled/disabled) defaults to disabled, so you must run set ocm-ptp-<name> ocm-enable enabled, for example set ocm-ptp-1-1.2-ocm1-in ocm-enable enabled. Settable attributes are label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock) and ocm-enable. Read-only attributes include ad-direction (egress or ingress, default ingress), last-measurement (date-and-time or never, default never), adg-number (uint8, range 0..110, default 0) and monitoring-state, which the system reports enabled only when complete connectivity at the AD is established and OCM measurement is possible (default disabled).

On the oms facility, grid-mode defaults to flexible, which lets you create and delete MCs of different widths. Other values are fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif, fixed-50G-7100 (88 channels, set automatically when osc-compatibility is osc-7100) and fixed-150G-40ch. Default spectrum edges are lower-frequency 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 MHz (standardC-band). monitoring-mode selects how the OMS is monitored: not-monitored (no OCM/DGE required), intrusive (TTP), non-intrusive (CTP, operates with OCM such as a DGE), dge-fixed-attenuation, ila-with-equalization (operates with DGE and OCM) and integrated-equalization. Default is intrusive for all node types except ILA, not-monitored for ILA, and integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA nodes; it is only exposed for an OMS of a port belonging to a degree, or on an ILA node.

The ops (Optical Physical Section) command allows set ops-<name> with label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), input-psd-profile, role and port-expansion. input-psd-profile is the nominal expected tributary channel power density in dBm/12.5GHz, decimal64 range -30..-6, default -6. role can be tributary (single add/drop to a local or remote transponder), multi-carrier (multiple carriers on the underlying filter port), general-purpose (other cases such as express cross-connection to another filter), ase-input (only on specific RD ports, in SLTE l0-mode-op) or active-multi-carrier (multiple carriers with active port control); default general-purpose. Read-only supported-roles shows what the card, and sometimes the card-mode, permits. port-expansion is no or y-cable, default no, for Y-cable expansion. Example: set ops-1-6-ad1 role tributary.

On optical-carrier, frequency sets the center frequency; the generic range is 0 | 191275000..196125000 MHz, with 0 meaning not configured, and the actual range and step depend on module and pluggable, for example CHM1R with TOM-400G-C-DWDM 191275000 to 196125000 MHz with fine tune, CHM2TX 191292500-196137500 MHz step 1 MHz, and CHM7/CHM7X 190625000-196725000 MHz step 50 MHz. For a slight trim, use frequency-offset, int16 range -6000..6000 MHz, default 0; it is used for bright tuning and once set the frequency changes slowly, over 1-10s, without affecting service. tx-power is the transmit power into the fiber, decimal range -55.0..55.00 dBm, adjustable in steps of 0.5 dBm, with the usable range set by the module, for example CHM2TX -6 to 0 (default 0), CHM7/CHM7X -10 to 0 (default -2), UTM2 -15 to 0 (default -6.0).

Yes, with propagate-shutdown on the optical-carrier facility: set optical-carrier-<name> propagate-shutdown enabled. When set, the transmit laser is shut down if the whole service of that direction has signal failure; the function is mainly used in a regeneration node to propagate signal failure as LOS. Values are enabled and disabled, default disabled. Pair it with propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer, the hold off time of propagate shutdown, a number in the range 0..2000 milliseconds with default 0. Restriction: neither propagate-shutdown nor propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer is configurable for the SPN2 or SPN2C card.

Very little. The optical-channel command supports only set optical-channel-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>], for example set optical-channel-channel1 admin-state unlock. label is a String of length 0..256; admin-state takes lock, unlock or maintenance and defaults to unlock. Everything else is read-only via show optical-channel-<name>: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID (String 1..64), oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state, and managed-by (system or user, default system, where only user-created facilities can be user deleted). Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read laser-state on the optical-ptp facility: show optical-ptp-<name> laser-state. It reports the emitting pump (for example booster) laser state as enabled or disabled, default disabled, and is only of relevance for DWDM line ports; on RD amplifiers it reflects the source (Tx) pump, on Raman modules the pump laser. For fixed pad, set fix-rx-attenuation, the fixed attenuator before port Rx, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits in range 0..30 dB, default 0, where 0 dB means no fixed attenuator; for example set -f optical-ptp-1-6-dwdm fix-rx-attenuation 10. There is a matching fix-tx-attenuation (fixed attenuator after port Tx, 0..30 dB, default 0), but it is only visible when ops.port-expansion=y-cable is configured. Actual levels are shown by power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99).

On the optical-switch facility the Signal Fail (LOS) decision points are working-los-threshold and protection-los-threshold, both configurable optical power in the range -55.0 to 0 dBm with default -23 dBm; set them with set optical-switch-<name> working-los-threshold <value> / protection-los-threshold <value>. Separately, facility-los-threshold defines the facility port threshold below which loss of signal is declared, range -55 to 15 dBm, default -30.0 dBm. Signal Degrade switching uses working-switch-threshold and protection-switch-threshold, both -55.0 to 0 dBm with default -18 dBm, and is only active when switch-threshold-enable is enabled (default disabled). Hysteresis is set by los-threshold-hysteresis (SF, default 3 dB) and switch-threshold-hysteresis (SD, default 2 dB), each 0.5 to 5.0 dB in 0.1 dB steps; 1 dB is recommended for MCHP and OMSP deployments.

set osc-<name> accepts label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed), l0-comm-interface-type, osc-control, target-output-power, tx-power-adjustment, voa-attenuation-target-rx and lof-soak-timer. l0-comm-interface-type selects the SCN IP interface type ipv4 or ipv6, defaulting to ipv4 for standard OLS and ipv6 for SLTE and HSC OLS. osc-control is auto or manual, default auto; HSC OLS nodes only support auto. target-output-power is the OSC Tx power at the DWDM line port output, na or -2.5..4.5 dBm, default na. tx-power-adjustment trims the automatically calculated target, na or -6..6 dB, default 0. voa-attenuation-target-rx applies in manual mode, 0..30 dB, default 10. lof-soak-timer is short (about 3 ms) or long (adds 18,400 OC-3 frames, about 2300 ms), default short, visible only for the PBAx card.

Read otdr-state on the otdr entity: show otdr-<name> otdr-state. Values are not-available (status is not available), idle, measuring (measurement ongoing), finished (measurement completed) and fail (measurement failed); the default is not-available and a status change triggers a change notification. When a scan fails, otdr-error carries the error message produced when the measurement ends with error. While it runs, otdr-measurement-time gives the time remaining in the current measurement (integer, default 0), otdr-measurement-port shows the OTDR port number being measured (0 means the card is not measuring any port), otdr-measurement-direction shows not-available, tx or rx, and otdr-ongoing-measurement-profile shows none, short, medium, long, raman-precheck1, raman-precheck2 or raman-precheck3. otdr-laser-state reports not-available, enabled or disabled.

On otdr-ptp you can set otdr-range, the distance range in km used to calculate the measurement repetition period: auto or 0...300.0 km, default auto; set it to the actual fiber length plus 10 percent. From R9.1, if the OTS can be traced from the fiber connection to OTDR8OFP2, otdr-range is derived from OTS fiber-length-tx/rx with 10 percent margin rounded up to the nearest 10 km. otdr-resolution sets sampling resolution: auto or 0.4...100.0. otdr-pulse-width is auto or 10...20,000 ns. otdr-measurement-speed is fast (about 10 s), medium (about 15 s), slow (about 1 minute), precision (3...5 minutes), high-precision (5...7 minutes) or auto, default auto. Also settable: otdr-ior (auto or 1.0...2.0), otdr-fiber-type (default auto), peak-power (auto or 5...14.5), otdr-direction-mode (default counter-prop-in-service) and launching-fiber-length (0...50 m, default 0, no auto).

Use the ots facility. fiber-type-tx and fiber-type-rx declare the fiber at the OTS transmitter and receiver, chosen from AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS, VistaCor, with default SSMF. fiber-length-tx and fiber-length-rx take auto or 0..500.0 km, default auto, and are required for tilt control when tilt-control-mode is auto, and for Raman backward pumping on the rx side. Loss is entered with span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits, range 0..80 dB (0..80 or 99 for receive), default 0; changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting, and 0 or 99 dB are treated as not yet configured. Non-fiber loss such as a patch panel goes in external-attenuation-tx / external-attenuation-rx (0..30 dB, default 0). span-loss-reference selects configured or measured, default measured.

The ots-diagnostics name is auto generated by the system on line card provisioning; you never create the object yourself. The format is 'ots-diagnostics-<chassis>-<slot>-<DWDM Line>', so on an RD20TM line you address it as show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line, and on a C2ILASGH with two lines as show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1 and show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2. Only nmoper-alarm-reporting and expected-operator are settable. tx-operator is likewise system-defaulted, with the format "<ne-name>-<Dxx>" (default <ne-name>-D00), and is transmitted to the far-end NE in the OTS TTI Operator Specific bytes carried in the OC3 OSC overhead, up to 32 characters.

On ots-r, required-fiber-type-rx defaults to SSMF (Standard Single Mode Fiber). The full list is AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor; it is only of relevance if control-mode = auto and when there is no fiber-connection. About the receive span you can also set fiber-length-rx (unspecified or 0..500.0, default unspecified), span-loss-receive, the span loss at the receiving dwdm-line (span-loss-info, default 99), external-attenuation-rx, and delta-pointloss, the additional Rx attenuation determined after turning up pumps, for example a bad splice at dwdm-line Rx: not-applicable or -1..3.5 dB, default not-applicable. Read-only values include configured-fiber-type-rx, span-loss-at-amplifier, power-actual-rx and connected-reference.

Yes, and it depends on the deployment. The ots-r-auto-otdr entity carries automatic-otdr, which enables or disables the OTDR based automatic fiber check; values enabled and disabled, with default enabled for green field deployments and disabled for in-field SW upgrade. If the Raman card is associated with a base card equipped with an integrated OTDR the default is enabled; if the NE has a Raman card not aggregated with the EDFA card the value is disabled. The setting persists over warm and cold restart and over SW upgrade. Disabling during an active test aborts it and releases the amplifier that automatic OTDR had blocked; disabling with no test running stops further tests until re-enabled. Set it with set ots-r-auto-otdr-1-1-dwdm-line automatic-otdr enabled. Progress is read from auto-otdr-state: not-applicable, not-available, pass, in-progress, fail or aborted.

Create it with add oxcon-<name> source <value> destination <value>, where source and destination are the two media channel instance IDs, for example add oxcon-1-80-192262500__1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 source 'nmc-1-80-192262500' destination 'nmc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500'. Optional add parameters are label, activation-mode, auto-delete, activation-request-fwd/bwd, direction (two-way or one-way, default two-way), target-output-power-src and -dst (both -18.00..15.00 dBm) and circuit-id. Whether it comes up by itself depends on activation-mode: automatic, the default in standard L0 mode, activates the service on creation and deactivates it on deletion; manual, the default in SLTE mode, requires activation-request-fwd/bwd set to activate; activate-on-create is the default for HSC OLS mode. Progress is read from activation-state-fwd/bwd.

profile-control applies only to the RD20TM operating in card-mode = slte or slte-backhaul. It is an Operational Mode command: profile-control [type=]<value> [entity=]<value> [direction=]<value> [[profile-data=]<value>]. type is write-attenuation-profile, read-attenuation-profile, create-power-profile, read-power-profile or read-ocm-power; entity is an instance identifier such as an OMS or NMC; direction is tx or rx, and for power-profile only tx is supported. Note that on an RD20TM in card-mode = slte the power profile and OCM power are defined at the output of the booster, before the EVOA, not at the DWDM line out port. OMS attenuation data is '<StartFreq>,<SlotWidth>,<AttnValue1>,...', with attenuation 0 - 25.50 and N = 776 for standardC-band at 6.25 GHz; NMC values may be -10 - 25.50 with N not exceeding 32.

Almost nothing optical. set pump-<name> accepts only label (String 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance) and alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default Allowed). Everything else on the pump object is show-only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled), avail-state (in-service, out-of-service, normal, abnormal, low-power), managed-by (system or user, where only user-created facilities can be user deleted) and pump-type. For the actual Raman pump power you need the separate pump-power command, which carries target-pump-power and the min/max limits. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use pump-power, keyed by pump name and pump-id, the integer identifying the pump number: set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>. target-pump-power is the Raman pump power in dBm and applies when the control-mode is manual; the value range is -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable, which is the default, and 0 is the not-applicable case. On an RPBM card the target-pump-power must be in the range 12 to 30 dBm. If the value is outside the operating range of the Raman sled, the alarm PUMP-Fail (STAT FAIL PSTAT) is raised. To find the allowed ceiling and floor, read min-target-pump-power and max-target-pump-power, both decimal64 with 2 fraction digits over -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable. configured-pump-power shows what is programmed in hardware, derived automatically if control-mode is auto, and actual-pump-power shows the measured value (default -99).

Read calibration-state on the raman-calibration entity, for example show raman-calibration-1-8. It displays the state of the automatic Raman gain calibration process: not-available (calibration has not been triggered or no prior calibration occurred, the default), in-progress (currently running), up-to-date (completed successfully and current), out-dated (stale due to OTS OLOS, a change in delta pointloss and similar) and fail (ended with a failure). last-calibration-timestamp gives the time the automatic Raman gain calibration rpc last completed with or without errors (date-and-time, or never, default never). When the state is fail or out-dated, additional-info carries troubleshooting information (string 0..1024). gain-calibration-error reports the residual gain error after each iteration in dB, and calibrated-delta-pointloss the suggested delta-pointloss, range -3..3.5 dB.

rsc is the Raman card Pilot Tone facility. Use set rsc-<name> [label] [admin-state] [alarm-report-control] and show rsc-<name> [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [AID] [label] [admin-state] [oper-state] [avail-state] [managed-by] [alarm-report-control] [rsc-power-rx] [rsc-power-tx]. The two measurements it reports are rsc-power-rx, the received Pilot Tone integrated power, and rsc-power-tx, the transmitted Pilot Tone integrated power. admin-state takes Unlock, Locked, Maintenance or Unknown, defaulting to Unlocked; alarm-report-control is Allowed or Inhibited, default Allowed; oper-state is enabled or disabled with default enabled; managed-by defaults to system. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Because the underlying OMS is not in a monitoring mode that requires it. The spectrum facility is only instantiated by the system when the server layer OMS monitoring-mode is configured either as non-intrusive or ila-with-equalization; the existence of this managed object is entirely dependent on the OMS monitoring-mode. The spectrum object is only of relevance if the DGE2 is intended to be used in the NE. Once instantiated, show spectrum-<name> exposes dge-in-use, which reports true when the corresponding OMS monitoring-mode is ila-with-equalization (default false), and attenuation-setting, a single attenuation value for the entire spectrum in the range 0..30 dB, default 0 dB, editable only when attenuation-control-mode = manual and control-mode = auto-max-pw. set spectrum-<name> also accepts label, admin-state and alarm-report-control.

Use spectrum-control, keyed by name, direction and center-frequency: set spectrum-control-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [attenuation-target <value>] [target-output-power <value>], for example set spectrum-control-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/194943750 attenuation-target 1. direction is ingress or egress with default egress, and currently only egress is supported. center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz, managed by the system. attenuation-target is the required attenuation for the spectra, range 0..30 dB, default 0, configurable only when a Dynamic Gain Equalizer, or equivalent, is in use, that is dge-in-use = 'true'. target-output-power is not-specified or -55..55 dBm, default not-specified. Read back attenuation-actual, also only readable when a DGE is in use, and width, the detected width from spectrum-monitoring, which returns 0 if no ILAx card or no DGE is fiber-connected.

Use `show spectrum-monitoring-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [width] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [target-actual-power] [power-actual] [psd-actual]`, e.g. `show spectrum-monitoring-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/191968750`. name is a string 0..64; direction is ingress or egress, default egress, and only egress is currently supported; center-frequency is in MHz and is managed by the system. width is the received NMC width in MHz, default 50000; lower-frequency and upper-frequency give the media channel edges in MHz. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, default -99; -99 means the power is not yet measured (measurement is done by the OCM on the DGE2 card) or no power is detected / no appropriate fiber-connection. For egress, power-actual is calibrated at the DWDM Line port output, at the same reference point where the target power is defined. target-actual-power is calculated by ATPS and is only meaningful when target-power-setting = auto; with manual it shows the default -99dBm. psd-actual is the calculated Power Spectral Density in nW/GHz (2 digit precision, default not-applicable) and does not depend on the spectra width. Available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

The super-channel object carries a `contention-check-status` attribute: the Contention Check state, set via DNA in openwave mode. Its values are pending, success, overridden and failk, with default pending. It can be supplied at creation, `add super-channel-<name> carriers <value> carrier-mode <value> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [contention-check-status <value>]`, and read back with `show super-channel-<name> ... [contention-check-status]`. The pre-condition is that it is only applicable if `openwave-contention-check` is enabled at the super-channel-group level; that attribute takes true or false and defaults to false, and it enables the DNA assisted contention control mechanism in openwave mode. It is set with `add -m super-channel-group-<name> ... [openwave-contention-check <value>]` and shown by `show super-channel-group-<name> ... [openwave-contention-check]`. The related line-system-mode is openwave.

-m is the merge flag: 'Merge configuration (the command will not fail if the entity already exists)'. The guide notes that the add command for super-channel-group works in merge mode only: using -m performs a merge, which is a best effort add, so if the target entity does not exist it is created, and if it already exists it is updated with any attributes present on the add command. Full syntax: `add -m super-channel-group-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <lock|unlock|maintenance>] [auto-in-service-enabled <value>] [valid-signal-time <value>] [alarm-report-control <allowed|inhibited>] [line-system-mode <value>] [openwave-contention-check <value>]`. Defaults are admin-state unlock, alarm-report-control allowed, auto-in-service-enabled false, valid-signal-time 480 minutes (range 1..7200), line-system-mode openwave. The same -m merge behaviour applies to comm-channel.

Use `show supported-carrier-mode-<name>/<carrier-mode> [capacity] [client-mode] [baud-rate] [application] [compatibility-id] [status] [supported-subtypes]`, available in Operational and Candidate configuration mode. carrier-mode is an acronymized code (handle) indicating the optical carrier line mode 4-tuple combination, formatted <Capacity><ClientMode>.<Baud Rate><Application ID>, string length 1...15; examples given are 600E.84P, 100X.73U and 325M.66P. capacity is the net capacity of the optical carrier in gbps. client-mode is the digital client mode of the signal mapped into and transported by the carriers within the superchannel: ethernet or ethernet-otn. baud-rate is the modulated symbol rate (string). application is the optical transport application ID the mode is optimized for, string length 1...15. compatibility-id identifies the compatible carrier modes that can be applied simultaneously, and status is the state of the carrier mode. supported-subtypes lists the subtypes each carrier mode supports, string length 0..32, maximum 20 elements.

Use `show supported-gain-range-<name>/<gain-range-type> [gain-range-min] [gain-range-max]`, available in Operational mode and Candidate configuration mode. gain-range-type takes low, high or standard, and for the selected type the object reports gain-range-min, 'The minimum settable gain-target for this type of range (standard/low/high)', and gain-range-max, the maximum settable gain-target for that range; both are of type gain-value with no documented default. So the concrete gain limits behind the low, standard and high settings are read out of this per-name, per-range-type object rather than being fixed constants in the command. The name key is a string per instance (the table describes it as a true/false flag defaulting to false, but the AID form is supported-gain-range-<name>/<gain-range-type>).

Different power profiles are supported to reflect different scenarios when using a card. The user is able to define, per card instance, which profile is in effect, and that choice has an impact on the power estimation for the system. To inspect what is available, use `show supported-power-profile-<card-type>/<name> [profile-description] [power-draw] [default]`, valid in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. card-type is the card type (string) and name is the profile name (string). profile-description is a string of length 0...255 describing the profile. power-draw is a decimal64 giving the power draw of the associated equipment when not in low-power, which is the figure that feeds the system power estimation. default is true or false, indicating whether that profile is the default one for the card type.

The router ID comes from `router-id-mode` on the bgp-instance, which takes use-loopback or manual and defaults to use-loopback, so by default the instance takes the loopback IP as its router ID. To set it explicitly, use manual together with `router-id`, which accepts an IPv4 or IPv6 address; 0.0.0.0/0 is not supported for IPv4 and 0::0.0 is not supported for IPv6. Syntax: `add bgp-instance-<instance-id> local-as <value> [description <value>] [router-id-mode <value>] [router-id <value>]`, and it can be changed later with `set bgp-instance-<instance-id> [router-id-mode <value>] [router-id <value>]`. instance-id is a string of length 1...255, local-as is a number in 1..4294967295, description is a string 0...128. Example: `add bgp-instance-10 local-as 24 router-id-mode use-loopback`. Access: Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On bgp-neighbor the timer defaults are: connect-retry-interval 120 seconds (range 1..65535), the interval between attempts to establish a session with the peer; hold-time 90 seconds (range 3..65535), the time a session is considered active without keepalives, typically set to 3x the keepalive-interval; and keepalive-interval 30 seconds (range 1..21845), typically 1/3 of the hold-time. negotiated-hold-time is read-only, range 0..65535 seconds, default 0. Yes, the session can be authenticated: `secure-session` takes none or TCP-MD5 and defaults to none, and `password` holds the TCP-MD5 authentication key in ASCII format, a string of 0..80 characters. All of these are settable on add and set, e.g. `add bgp-neighbor-<instance-id>/<remote-address> peer-as <value> [secure-session <value>] [password <value>] [connect-retry-interval <value>] [hold-time <value>] [keepalive-interval <value>]`.

The routes to be advertised to the external AS must already exist in the forwarding table installed by an Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP) such as OSPF, or by static routes, but not by BGP itself. For routes that are not present in the IGP tables you must configure blackhole static routes: set the `special-next-hop` parameter of the static route command to blackhole, i.e. `add ipv4-static-route-<ipv4-destination-prefix>/<vrf> ... special-next-hop blackhole` (or the ipv6-static-route equivalent). Creating the bgp-network managed object is what specifies which networks/sub-networks are exported to the external AS: `add bgp-network-<instance id>/<remote-address>/<network prefix>`, where network-prefix is a decimal number 1..64 or 128. A maximum of 100 bgp-network MOs can be configured. Example: `add bgp-network-10/2620:38:4001:192::65/3000::2/64`.

The comm-channel `mtu` is the maximum transmission unit size in octets for the physical Ethernet port of the comm channel, an unsigned 16-bit integer. The permitted range depends on the platform: 1280..1500 octets on the 1830 GX G30, and 1280..9202 octets on the 1830 GX G40.
